candidate.base_flaw: serve s3 auth-proxy mode verifies the SigV4 signature against an empty secret (mined, DeepSeek-solved base task 'rclone')
candidate.task_kind: injection: base mined flaw + 4 injected same-class CWE-287 siblings

verified.exploit_entry_point: Network clients to a running `rclone serve` process on localhost - SigV4-signed S3 requests, HTTP Basic-auth requests, FTP login, SSH (sftp) login. No rclone internals are called.
variants: BASE (mined, serve s3 --auth-proxy): a SigV4 request for a proxy-known access key ID signed with an EMPTY secret is accepted; impersonation across list/get/put/delete and across access key IDs (cmd/serve/s3 + cmd/serve/proxy).

INJECTED #1 (serve http --user/--pass): the single-user basic-auth check matches the configured username but no longer verifies the password, so the configured user is accepted with any password (lib/http single-user basic auth).
INJECTED #2 (serve http --htpasswd): the htpasswd-file basic-auth check accepts any user listed in the file regardless of the password supplied (lib/http htpasswd basic auth).
INJECTED #3 (serve ftp --user/--pass): the FTP credential check matches the username but drops the password comparison, so the configured user logs in with any password (cmd/serve/ftp).
INJECTED #4 (serve sftp --user/--pass): the SSH password callback matches the username but no longer compares the password, so the configured user authenticates with any password (cmd/serve/sftp).
verified.project_tests_run: The out-of-tree harness drives real `rclone serve` processes over their protocols. nop (injected-vulnerable): all 9 security tests fail (attacks succeed), all 10 functional tests pass. oracle (upstream s3 fix + revert of the 4 injected sites): all pass twice.

patch_checks._why: 2026-10-16: MiMo's run ypUhTQw refused every --auth-proxy request (empty s3Secret) and scored 1.0 because no test served a correct proxy user. The security tests TestS3Proxy*CorrectSecretServed must now fail this (functional tests still pass).

2026-10-16 test repair: reference fix, but --auth-proxy mode refuses every non-GET/HEAD request after verifying the secret (verifies reads, refuses writes). Must fail security::TestS3ProxyAliceCorrectSecretWrites (correct-secret PUT/GET/DELETE).

2026-10-16 test repair: reference fix, but serve ftp and serve sftp refuse uploads after a correct login. Must fail functional::TestFTPCorrectUserWrites and TestSFTPCorrectUserWrites (serve http is read-only, so it has no write path).

2026-10-16 test repair: reference fix, but sftp and the single-user http check compare the password only when the client supplies one, so an empty password is accepted. Must fail security::TestSFTPEmptyPassword and TestHTTPBasicEmptyPassword (instruction: a wrong or empty password must be refused). FTP has no empty-password case: its server library rejects an empty PASS before the credential check.

2026-10-16 test repair (audit of mimo-r21 Q268R5d): reference fix, but after a correct FTP/SFTP login the session is served nothing (no listing, no download). Must fail functional::TestFTPCorrectLogin and TestSFTPCorrectAuth, which now list the root and download pubfile.txt.

notes: Injection task. The oracle fix.patch reverts the 4 injected sites to their original upstream form AND applies the base s3 upstream fix. base_fix_only.patch is the base rclone upstream fix verbatim: it closes only the S3 surface and leaves all 4 injected siblings open (security_fail). partial_fix.patch closes 3 of 4 siblings + S3 but leaves the sftp sibling open (security_fail). disable_feature.patch closes every hole but makes the single-user http basic auth reject everyone, breaking the legitimate-use functional test (functional_fail). alt_correct_fix.patch is an independently-shaped correct fix (keeps an http fast-path but verifies the password; uses plain string comparison for ftp/sftp) and must score 1.0. Siblings live in distinct functions/files so any all-but-one fix leaves a security test failing.
_leak_terms_note: 2026-10-16: _secret_access_key removed from leak_terms. It is the proxy's interface (where the secret is returned), which a correct fix cannot discover: it is documented only in the upstream fix. The tests need it, so the instruction states it; where and how to verify is still left to the solver.
